say: Tap both shoulders hard and shout.
Do they respond?
Watch their chest.
Gasping is not breathing.
Are they breathing normally?
steps.quote: The No-No-Go framework is reiterated as an effective method for recognizing OHCA.

say: Point at one person.
Say: you, bring the A E D.
steps.quote: A simplified visual aid for lay rescuers emphasizes early activation of the EMS system and obtaining an automated external defibrillator in addition to initiation of chest compressions.

steps.sub: On their back. Kneel at the chest.
say: Lay them flat on their back, on the floor.
Kneel beside their chest.
steps.quote: For adult cardiac arrest, rescuers should perform chest compressions with the patient on a firm surface and with the patient's torso at approximately the level of the rescuer's knees.

steps.sub: Center of the chest. Arms straight.
say: Heel of one hand on the center of the chest.
Other hand on top. Arms straight.
steps.note: Not yet quoted. Confirm the 2025 Part 7 hand-position sentence (heel of one hand, center of the chest / lower half of the sternum) in a browser.

say: Are you trained and willing to give breaths?
If not, hands only.
steps.quote: It is reasonable for lay rescuers and health care professionals to perform CPR with cycles of 30 compressions followed by 2 breaths before placement of an advanced airway. [...] Telecommunicators [...] are to guide lay rescuers to use Hands-Only CPR for adults.

steps.sub: About 2 inches. Let it come back up.
say: Push hard and fast. Follow the beat.
reminders: Has anyone found an A E D?
Let the chest come all the way up.
breathsSay: Tilt the head. Lift the chin.
steps.quote: During manual CPR, rescuers should perform chest compressions to a depth of at least 2 inches, or 5 cm, for an average adult while avoiding excessive chest compression depths (greater than 2.4 inches, or 6cm). [...] rescuers perform chest compressions at a rate of 100 to 120/min.

say: Keep pushing while someone opens it.
Turn it on. Follow its voice.
steps.quote: Early high-quality CPR and prompt defibrillation are the most important interventions associated with improved outcomes in adult cardiac arrest.

steps.sub: A bra can be moved aside.
say: Bare the chest. Pads where the pictures show.
You can move a bra aside. No need to remove it.
steps.quote: When placing pads for defibrillation for an adult in cardiac arrest, it might be reasonable to adjust the position of a bra instead of removing it.

say: Hands off while it analyzes.
If it says shock, everyone stand clear.
steps.note: Not yet quoted. Confirm the 2025 Part 7 AED sequence (follow prompts, no one touching during analysis/shock, resume compressions immediately) in a browser.

say: Roll them onto their side to drain it.
Wipe the mouth. Roll back. Keep pushing.
steps.note: MedlinePlus says to roll the whole body to the side if the person vomits; the fetch tool paraphrased it, so the exact sentence still needs copying from the page.

say: They're responding. Don't start compressions.
Stay with them. Watch their breathing.
steps.quote: Check the person's airway, breathing, and pulse frequently. If necessary, begin CPR.
